about: Verbatim excerpts from every source this guide cites, saved so each fact can be traced and re-checked. Excerpts are short; see each URL (and its archived copy, when added) for full context.

excerpts.quote: These bridges are currently owned, operated, and maintained by the USACE.
excerpts.supports: USACE owns, operates and maintains both bridges

excerpts.quote: Currently, the roadways of both bridges consist of two lanes in each direction with a sidewalk on one side.
excerpts.supports: Two travel lanes in each direction on each bridge

excerpts.quote: Traffic delays are prevalent during the summer with frequent traffic backups.

sources.title: Cape Cod Bridges Program Final Environmental Impact Statement, Chapter 1: Introduction

excerpts.quote: Sagamore Bridge is 1,408 feet long with three spans, carrying U.S. Route 6 across Cape Cod Canal
Bourne Bridge is 2,384 feet long with seven spans, carrying State Route 28 across Cape Cod Canal
Each bridge is 48 feet, 8 inches wide, including four 10-foot-wide vehicular travel lanes
which opened to traffic in June 1935.
excerpts.supports: Both bridges opened to traffic in June 1935

excerpts.quote: These bridges — which provide the only roadway connections between Cape Cod and the mainland — are currently owned by the United States
excerpts.supports: Only roadway connections between Cape Cod and the mainland

sources.title: Notice of Final Federal Agency Actions on Proposed Transportation Project in Massachusetts (FR Doc. 2026-17969)

excerpts.quote: Final Environmental Impact Statement (FEIS) and Record of Decision (ROD) for the Project, signed June 26, 2026,
The actions relate to the proposed Cape Cod Bridges Project which includes replacement of the Sagamore Bridge carrying U.S. Route 6
excerpts.supports: Project includes replacing the Sagamore Bridge

excerpts.quote: and replacement of the Bourne Bridge carrying State Route 28 as it travels across the Cape Cod Canal
excerpts.supports: Project includes replacing the Bourne Bridge

sources.title: Cape Cod Canal Transportation Study, Chapter 2: Existing Environmental and Traffic Conditions

excerpts.quote: The summer period data collection occurred August 10–17 and the non summer collection took place October 19–26, as these months were found to be representative of these periods.
excerpts.supports: Summer counts in August, non-summer counts in October (2014, per Table 2-16 headings)
Table 2-16 (2014): Bourne summer PM and Saturday peak hours 4,750, summer ADT 56,500, non-summer 38,000; Sagamore Saturday peak hour 5,800, summer ADT 65,900, non-summer 41,400

excerpts.quote: daily traffic volumes on the Bourne and Sagamore Bridge are 49% and 59% higher in the summer, respectively, compared to non-summer periods.
the average traffic volumes crossing the Canal Bridges during February are only 54% (Bourne Bridge) to 60% (Sagamore Bridge) of the volumes crossing these bridges during August.
Traffic data was collected for summer Saturday peak period, a period of high traffic demand ... because vacation rentals on the Cape generally begin and end on Saturday.
The time periods examined were: AM summer weekday (7:00 AM – 9:00 AM) PM summer weekday (4:00 PM – 6:00 PM) Saturday summer (10:00 AM - 12:00 PM)
excerpts.supports: 2014 study periods: weekday 7-9 AM and 4-6 PM; Saturday 10 AM-12 PM
